item.title: Lack of street lights in park area, 17th September
item.description:
I am writing to raise a serious concern regarding the lack of adequate lighting at Longlands Recreation Park. I am a young woman who regularly uses the park to walk my dog, and I know that many other local residents — including women, dog walkers and families — also rely on the park as part of our local community. However, as the evenings are becoming darker earlier, the severe lack of lighting is making the park increasingly difficult and frightening to use. Once it becomes dark, there are large areas of the park that are extremely poorly lit, particularly around the trees and less visible sections of the paths. This leaves people feeling vulnerable and creates areas where someone could potentially be hiding without being seen. As a young woman walking alone, I should be able to use my local park without feeling that I am putting myself at risk simply by taking my dog for a walk. This is particularly concerning given the wider concerns around women’s safety and the number of incidents we hear about in the news. I appreciate that a lack of lighting does not necessarily prevent crime, but appropriate lighting can improve visibility and help residents feel safer when using public spaces after dark. I also understand that installing additional lighting needs to take neighbouring properties into consideration. However, there are already lights distributed around the park, and many neighbouring properties have trees and other natural screening. I would therefore ask the Council to properly assess whether additional, appropriately positioned lighting could be installed without causing unreasonable disturbance to nearby residents. Modern, directional or lower-level lighting may also provide a possible solution while limiting light spill into surrounding properties. Residents pay council tax and should reasonably expect our public spaces, parks and facilities to be maintained to a standard that allows us to use them safely. It is incredibly frustrating to feel that we cannot properly enjoy a local green space because of inadequate lighting. I would therefore ask Bexley Council to: * Carry out a safety and lighting assessment of Longlands Recreation Park, particularly along the main walking routes and darker sections. * Consider installing additional appropriately positioned lighting where there are significant gaps. * Consider lighting solutions designed to minimise light pollution and disturbance to neighbouring properties. * Take into account the concerns of local women, dog walkers and other residents who use the park during the darker hours. * Provide residents with information on whether improvements to the park’s lighting are currently being considered or planned. I would appreciate this concern being taken seriously and would welcome a response explaining what action the Council can take to improve safety at Longlands Recreation Park. Local residents should be able to use their local park without fear simply because the sun has gone down. Kind regards,

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Appledore Crescent, Longlands, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Copy and paste these exact entries directly into the form fields: Summarise the problem Severe structural pavement failure & active trip hazard outside 49 fairford Avenue, 17th September
item.description:
I am reporting an active, unmitigated trip hazard and structural footway failure on the shared dropped kerb outside 49 fairford Avenue The asphalt layer exhibits extensive sub-base degradation and deep "alligatoring" cracking. Recent council works addressed only the adjacent half of this continuous surface. Leaving half of a visibly failed surface unaddressed is technically flawed; unsealed cracks next to the new patch permit lateral water ingress, which will lead to total surface collapse during approaching winter freeze-thaw cycles. This footway sits on a high-footfall route heavily used by school children, parents with prams and elderly residents. Unrepaired, it poses an immediate injury risk and elevates the council's public liability exposure under Section 41 of the Highways Act 1980. Preventative resurfacing is urgently required. Photos attached. Many thanks. Mr Michael S Nuno (MEng/GMICE)

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Fairford Avenue, Barnehurst, Greater London

item.title: Sapling planted circa 2018 fronting the chemist shop at 171 High St Beckenham, 4 metres from the junction with Village Way - the inextensible tree tie and tarmac are now strangling the expanding trunk., 16th September
item.description:
Sapling planted circa 2018 fronting the chemist shop at 171 High St Beckenham, 4 metres from the junction with Village Way - the inextensible tree tie and tarmac are now strangling the expanding trunk. The sapling is now about 4 inches (10cm) in diameter and is fully self supporting. Please remove the 'strangling' black tree ties, the pair of stakes and remove a ring of tarmac from ground level to let the poor tree grow without mutilation. This and other saplings were planted as part of the £4.4m Circa 2018 Beckenham Town Centre Improvement Scheme. A new location will have to be found for what looks like a planning application notice, if it is still applicable.
